questions.question: Define a DP table for max contiguous subarray sum.
questions.expected: `OPT[j] = max sum of a contiguous subarray ending at index j`.

questions.question: Write the recurrence for 0-1 Knapsack.
questions.expected: `OPT[j, Z] = max(OPT[j-1, Z], v_j + OPT[j-1, Z - w_j])`. Base case `OPT[0, Z] = 0`.

questions.question: What are the four required parts of a DP exam answer?
questions.expected: (i) Table definition; (ii) recurrence + correctness; (iii) bottom-up algorithm + runtime; (iv) reconstruction.

questions.question: True or False: 0-1 Knapsack with weight capacity W has runtime O(nW), which is polynomial in the input size.
questions.expected: False. W is given as a number; its encoding takes log W bits. O(nW) is exponential in log W, so the algorithm is pseudo-polynomial, not polynomial.

questions.question: Which DP recurrence correctly solves Weighted Interval Scheduling (where p(i) is the latest interval finishing before i starts)?
Items with (value, weight): (60, 3), (100, 5), (120, 4). Capacity W = 7. What is the optimal 0/1 Knapsack value? Show your reasoning briefly.
questions.expected: Optimal: choose item 1 (60, 3) and item 3 (120, 4): total weight 7, value 180. Other feasible subsets: just item 2 = 100; items 1+2 = weight 8 (infeasible). Answer: 180.
